Amadeus Pune._comment: Amadeus Pune — from the client's sample week (docs/pune_client_logic.md). Seven service days: Mon-Fri full, Saturday drops the veg dry, Sunday is flavoured rice (a veg biryani) with raita, papad, buttermilk and a sweet and nothing else. The raita comes from the Curd / Raita category the client configured, restricted to Sunday — the day the biryani wants it.

rules._comment: 'flavour rice on Tue and sun' — the flavoured-rice slot runs on those two days only. Every other day's rice row is the white_rice constant.
rules.name: amadeus_pune_flavour_rice_tue_sun

rules._comment: 'white rice daily', but the sample week's single rice row shows ONE rice per day: Tue is Coriander rice and Sun is Veg biryani, with steamed rice on the other five. So white rice runs on exactly the days the flavoured-rice slot does NOT (Mon, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat) — it used to include Tue, which put Tawa Pulao AND steamed rice on the same day. Kept as a weekday list rather than a rule keyed off the flavoured-rice slot because both slots are day-restricted to fixed weekdays; if 'flavour rice on Tue and sun' ever changes, this list changes with it.
rules.name: amadeus_pune_white_rice_off_on_flavour_rice_days

rules._comment: 'sat no veg dry it should be blank' — and Sunday serves no veg dry either.
rules.name: amadeus_pune_veg_dry_weekdays_only

rules._comment: The sample's Sunday salad column is the raita, not a salad, so the salad slot stops at Saturday and `curd_side` covers Sunday.
rules.name: amadeus_pune_salad_mon_sat

rules._comment: Curd / Raita runs on Sunday only — the biryani day, which is the classic pairing and the only day the sample shows it. The Pune curd_side pool is two raitas (raita, boondi_raita) and the solver picks one, so this is a real ontology dish with a colour and a history entry rather than the stamped 'Raita' string it replaced. Widen allowed_weekdays if the client wants curd or raita on more days.
rules.name: amadeus_pune_curd_side_sunday_only

rules._comment: 'chapati daily in indain bread' — a per-day MANDATE, not merely permission to repeat. On a one-slot family a slot_composition component with count 1 means 'this slot must be a matching dish', so bread is chapati on every day it is served. fixed_daily_item was the wrong tool: it only makes the matching dish CONSISTENT across days and leaves the solver free to serve phulka instead, which it did. The city ruleset's plain_chapati_may_repeat supplies the unique_items / cooldown exemption the repetition needs.
rules.name: amadeus_pune_chapati_daily

rules._comment: Buttermilk runs every day, so it must be exempt from unique_items and from the 20-day cooldown. The city ruleset declares no welcome-drink staple (R59 was ambiguous until this client answered it), so the declaration is scoped here.
rules.name: amadeus_pune_buttermilk_is_a_staple

rules._comment: 'welcome drink will have butter milk daily' — the client's answer to the Pune rulebook's R59: the welcome drink IS the buttermilk, not an extra accompaniment. Same one-slot mandate as the bread above.
rules.name: amadeus_pune_buttermilk_daily

rules._comment: 'weekly 1 panner' — exactly one paneer dish a week, counted across every slot (the Pune list has 13 paneer gravies and one paneer-based veg dry).
rules.name: amadeus_pune_paneer_weekly

rules._comment: 'weekly 1 soya' — the sample's soya is a veg DRY (Monday's Soya Chatpata Dry), and all three of Pune's is_premium_veg_dry items are the soya dries, so this is also what makes the city ruleset's premium_veg_dry_weekly cap non-vacuous. Scoped to veg_dry on that reading; drop the base_slot if the client is happy with a soya gravy instead.
rules.name: amadeus_pune_soya_veg_dry_weekly

rules._comment: …and no SECOND soya dish anywhere else that week (the Pune list has one soya gravy, soya_masala). The pair together mean 'exactly one soya a week, and it is the veg dry'.
rules.name: amadeus_pune_soya_total_weekly

rules._comment: 'in sun we server only flvour rice(any veg biryani)' — Sunday's rice must be a veg biryani, and 'any' is why this is a composition over the biryani flag rather than a pinned dish: the solver picks between veg_biryani and handi_biryani. Only `sun` is listed, so no other day gets a mandated component. One biryani day also satisfies the city ruleset's mixedveg_pulao_biryani_weekly cap of one.
rules.name: amadeus_pune_sunday_veg_biryani
